messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: inference-api p99 latency breach (SLO burn 12% > 10%) - pager: PD#INC-4521 - https://pagerduty.com/INC-4521 :rotating_light:
devon: ack - I'm oncall and taking initial triage
alex: oncall-sr here, joining the thread
pagerduty-bot: PD: INC-4521 acknowledged by devon@redwood
devon: quick glance: tail spiking only in eu-west. heatmap shows KV cache evictions coincident with canary deploy (deploy id=deploy-2026-03-15-21). p95 mostly fine, p99 jumps ~300-500ms
maria: any error 5xxs? customer-reported timeouts?
devon: small increase in timeouts, ~1.4% overall, a few 504s from sidecar queue. Logs snippet:
```
[eu-west-1] 2026-03-15T21:03:12Z inference-api ERROR evict_key key=usr:session:abcd ttl=0 cause=cache-pressure
[eu-west-1] 2026-03-15T21:03:13Z inference-api WARN sidecar_queue length=512 max=512 drop=12
[eu-west-1] 2026-03-15T21:03:14Z inference-api INFO request latency p99=920ms p95=120ms
```
ops-bot: autoscaler: +2 replicas requested for inference-runtime-eu-west (reason: queue-backpressure). Scaling started at 21:04:02Z
alex: looks like last canary increased prefix diversity -> cache miss rate skyrocketed, evictions thrash sidecars. two mitigations: 1) rollback canary 2) route a subset of traffic to fallback model or different region. Which do we want fast?
maria: rollback is safest if canary is the culprit. canary batch started at 20:58Z so rollback should be quick. but if rollback takes time, we can enable model-fallback for >= 500ms requests to avoid timeouts.
devon: initiating rollback now: kubectl rollout undo deploy/inference-canary --namespace=prod-eu-west (running)
ops-bot: rollout undo accepted for inference-canary (uid=abc123)
devon: also toggling traffic-routing for urgent calls -> temporary route to gpt-small-v2 for latency-sensitive customers. curl to flip route:
```
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/route -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"gpt-small-v2","match":{"latency_threshold_ms":500}}'
```
pagerduty-bot: PD: INC-4521 escalation to oncall-sr (alex) after ack window - notified alex@redwood
alex: I'm taking over command. devon, what's ETA on rollback finish?
devon: rollout complete at 21:07:46Z. old replicas back in place. preliminary metrics show reduced evictions but p99 still elevated ~160-200ms above baseline
maria: we increased sidecar queue size and extended KV cache TTL to 8s (temporary). config patch applied:
```
ENV: KV_CACHE_TTL=8s
ENV: SIDECAR_MAX_QUEUE=1024
```
devon: applying cache config now - patch rolled at 21:09:30Z
ops-bot: config rollout succeeded, new sidecar queue limit active in eu-west
devon: within 6 minutes p99 trending down. current p99=210ms (baseline ~90ms). SLO burn dropped from 12% -> 4%
alex: good. customer impact summary so far: ~3 customers reported UI timeouts (support tickets created: #SUP-998, #SUP-1001, #SUP-1004). no major data loss, degraded experience only.
maria: created incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OPS-1287 - assigned to infra/serving for postmortem. priority=P2
oncall-sr: handing off monitoring to maria for next 3h window. i'll stay on-call for any regression until 22:00Z then silent handover. maria, confirm you have alert playbook?
maria: got it. will monitor p99, error rate, and sidecar queue. enabling additional dashboard alert: p99 > 250ms -> ping eng-sre.
devon: notes for postmortem: probable root cause = increased prefix diversity from canary model variant causing KV cache miss storm + insufficient per-key locking -> eviction thrash. immediate resolution: rollback canary + increase TTL + route fallback + autoscaler. followups: quantify cache hit delta, add canary throttling, add circuit-breaker on sidecar queue, and add runbook for canary traffic ramp.
alex: agree. will draft timeline and owner list. did we need to keep PD incident open? current status: mitigated but monitoring.
maria: keep PD open until stable for 1h. I'll close after verification window.
incident-bot: PD: INC-4521 status updated -> mitigated; ack still active; awaiting manual close
devon: thanks team. final check: p99=110ms now, SLO burn=1.2% - within limits. will add measurement segments and synth tests for eu-west.
alex: excellent work. please add any missing logs and snapshots to OPS-1287. I'll take the lead on the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
maria: handing off to night shift monitoring. leaving notes in the ticket.
incident-bot: Thread closed for updates? (automated reminder will ping in 30m)
